title: Core Terraform workflow
subtitle: Review plans, apply deliberately, and replace safely.

delta.before: You may remember taint and imperative refresh habits.
delta.after: Use saved plans, -replace and -refresh-only with precise exit-code checks.

exercises.title: CLI Flag Lab
exercises.description: Choose the command that matches the operational intent.

cases.prompt: Replace only a damaged security group after reviewing a saved plan.
cases.explanation: Apply the reviewed tfplan; replacement is a planned infrastructure action.

cases.prompt: Accept observed remote changes into state without changing infrastructure.
cases.explanation: Refresh-only updates state and outputs, not the desired HCL or cloud objects.

cases.prompt: Check formatting in CI without rewriting files.
cases.explanation: The -check flag reports differences without formatting the files.

cost.assumptions: Short-lived resources, no compute, standard parameters, no uploads; gross usage before account credits.

checkpoints.prompt: A fresh checkout is missing modules/providers. Which sequence prepares and checks it before approving infrastructure changes?

choices.a: Initialize, validate configuration, then generate and review a plan
choices.b: Apply immediately, then format and delete state

rationale.a: Init installs dependencies; validation checks consistency; planning exposes the intended changes.
rationale.b: This skips preparation/review and risks losing management relationships.

checkpoints.prompt: Which command applies the exact saved plan named reviewed.plan?

rationale.a: A positional saved-plan path applies that reviewed artifact.
rationale.b: -out is a plan flag, not an apply flag.

checkpoints.prompt: Which operation removes managed infrastructure, and why does fmt -check not replace it?

choices.a: Destroy removes managed objects; fmt -check only checks source formatting
choices.b: fmt -check deletes resources after rewriting their files

rationale.a: Formatting does not execute infrastructure deletion.
rationale.b: The check flag neither rewrites files nor destroys cloud objects.
